backlog.spec: Replace the binary ECFP/FCFP bit vectors with hashed count vectors. Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=3, fpSize=N_BITS) and call GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy for both the ECFP and FCFP generators in featurize, instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy. Counts carry occupancy information that bit vectors lose, which helps tree models on logD. For the Tanimoto kernel, switch to the count-based (min/max) Tanimoto: sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)), computed with a vectorized approach on the float64 ECFP count matrix, or keep the existing bit-based Tanimoto if the min/max version is too slow. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints at radius 3

backlog.spec: In base_predict, train the RandomForest and LightGBM with 3 different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2). For LightGBM also use bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1. Average each learner's predictions over the seeds before they enter the stack. Reduce RF to 150 trees per seed to keep the runtime similar. The kernel member stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-seed averaging of tree base learners

backlog.spec: In base_predict, replace the RandomForestRegressor with sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed). ExtraTrees usually extrapolates more smoothly on fingerprint plus descriptor features and is faster. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Replace RF with ExtraTrees on min_samples_leaf=2

backlog.spec: Compute Crippen MolLogP for each molecule. Train the base models on y - a*logP, where a comes from a linear fit of y on logP over the training fold. Add it back at prediction. Do this inside base_predict, or simply give the models a lower-variance target. Keep the descriptors as features.
backlog.title: Crippen/MolLogP-residual target

backlog.spec: Set the LGB learning_rate to 0.02 and N_ROUNDS to 1200. Add lambda_l2=5, min_child_samples=15, feature_fraction=0.15, and use the huber objective (alpha=1.0) instead of regression_l1. Keep the rest unchanged and check the time budget.
backlog.title: LightGBM tuning: lower LR, more rounds, stronger regularization

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after the first oof stack pass, form soft targets y_s = 0.5 * y + 0.5 * oof_meta, where oof_meta is the meta-learner prediction on the out-of-fold matrix. Refit the whole stack once with y_s as the training target for base_predict in each fold, while the meta-learner is still fit against the original y. Final test predictions come from the refit base learners combined with the same meta weights. This is one extra pass through the stack, so reduce the inner Tanimoto grid if the job approaches the time limit.
backlog.title: Self-distillation of training targets

backlog.spec: The stack already produces an out-of-fold matrix of base predictions for every training molecule. Use it to correct any systematic bias in the final output: apply the fitted meta-learner to the out-of-fold matrix to obtain one out-of-fold stacked prediction per training molecule, then fit sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip', increasing=True) mapping those out-of-fold predictions to the true targets, and pass the test-set stacked predictions through the fitted isotonic map before returning them. Because the calibrator is fitted on scaffold-grouped out-of-fold values it cannot leak within-fold information. Keep the uncalibrated prediction as a fallback if the isotonic fit raises.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold isotonic recalibration of the stacked prediction

backlog.spec: In base_predict, average 3 LightGBM models trained with seeds seed, seed+1 and seed+2 (use bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1 for diversity). Raise the RF to 400 trees with min_samples_leaf=1 and max_features=0.2. This reduces variance in the base predictions fed to the meta learner.
backlog.title: Multi-seed RF and LGB averaging

backlog.spec: The metric is MAE but the stacker minimizes squared error. Replace meta = Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True).fit(oof, y) with an L1 meta-learner: sklearn.linear_model.QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=0.0, solver='highs').fit(oof, y). Then clip negative coefficients to zero: if any coef_ < 0, refit on only the columns with positive weights (keep a column mask and apply it to base_te at predict time). Return meta.predict(base_te[:, mask]).
backlog.title: MAE meta-learner with intercept

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge(positive=True) meta learner with a stacker fit on the out-of-fold predictions that minimizes MAE. Use scipy.optimize.minimize over simplex weights (softmax parametrization) on the L1 loss of the OOF predictions. This matches the MAE metric and avoids the 1e-3 ridge shrinkage.
backlog.title: Nonnegative meta stacker with bias and CV-selected shrinkage

backlog.spec: Several entries in this kind of data set are salts or charged forms, so the same parent molecule can produce different fingerprints and descriptors. Add a cached helper that, for each SMILES, parses the molecule, keeps only the largest fragment by heavy-atom count (split on '.' or use rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags), then neutralises the common ionised groups by applying rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and returns the canonical SMILES of the result. Route every call that currently does Chem.MolFromSmiles -- in featurize, desc_vector and the Murcko scaffold computation -- through this cleaned structure. Cache per input SMILES because the same molecules recur across the fifteen fits. If standardisation raises for a molecule, fall back to the original parse.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and charge neutralisation before featurising

backlog.spec: In featurize, use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy for both the ECFP and FCFP generators, and clip counts at 255 (float32). The tree models then see counts. In base_predict, replace the tanimoto() kernel on Fa/Fb with the MinMax (generalized Tanimoto) kernel: K(a,b)=sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)). Compute it memory-efficiently by looping over chunks of 256 rows of A (np.minimum(A_chunk[:,None,:],B[None,:,:]).sum(-1) is too large for 1024 columns, so instead use the identity sum(max)=sum(a)+sum(b)-sum(min). Compute sum(min) by expanding counts into thresholded binary planes: for t in 1..max_count (cap at 8 by clipping counts at 8 for the kernel only), sum(min)=sum_t (A>=t)@(B>=t).T). Everything else stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Count Morgan fingerprints + MinMax kernel

backlog.spec: Add the 167 MACCS keys (from rdkit.Chem import MACCSkeys; np.array(MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol)), cached per SMILES) as a separate block. Append it to Xtr/Xte after the descriptor block, and in base_predict change the descriptor slice to Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:2*N_BITS+n_desc] (pass n_desc = len(Descriptors._descList)). Also add a fourth base learner: sklearn.svm.SVR(C=5.0, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') fit on the standardized descriptor block Za concatenated with the MACCS block. Its prediction is a fourth column, and oof gets 4 columns.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and descriptor-only SVR

backlog.spec: Append the 167-bit MACCS structural keys as an extra block: from rdkit.Chem import MACCSkeys, then for each molecule use np.array(MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol), dtype=np.float32) (or GetFingerprintAsNumPy on the returned ExplicitBitVect). Compute it inside featurize alongside the Morgan fingerprints and hstack it after the existing fingerprint columns and before the descriptor block. Because base_predict slices descriptors as Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:], update that slice index to 2*N_BITS + 167 so the descriptors are still the block passed to the RBF kernel. The Tanimoto kernel should remain on the ECFP bits only.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys to the feature matrix

backlog.spec: Append rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_ (42 features), Crippen per-atom-type contributions via rdMolDescriptors, and the counts of the 2D pharmacophore feature types to desc_vector. Cache them as before. They then go through the same percentile clipping and feed all models.
backlog.title: Extra RDKit descriptors: MQN and fragment counts

backlog.spec: Add sklearn MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, max_iter=300, random_state=seed). Train it on the standardized descriptors Za and the first 1024 ECFP bits, and average 3 seeds. Add its predictions as an extra column in base_predict and make oof 4 columns wide.
backlog.title: Add an MLP base learner

backlog.spec: Add a fourth base learner in base_predict: a CatBoostRegressor with loss_function='MAE', iterations=800, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0, trained on Xa and ya, predicting Xb. Return it as an extra column in the np.column_stack output, so the oof matrix in fit_predict becomes 4 columns wide (change np.zeros((len(y), 3)) to 4). Watch the time budget: the nested stacking calls base_predict 6 times per fit, so keep CatBoost fast (for example depth 6 and about 800 iterations on 3360 rows). If the total job time nears 10 minutes, drop the CatBoost iterations to 500.
backlog.title: CatBoost base learner with MAE loss

backlog.spec: Use calculated logP as a physics prior. In fit_predict, compute c = Crippen.MolLogP for each train and test molecule (from rdkit.Chem import Crippen; cache per SMILES like the descriptors). Fit a 1-D Huber regression (sklearn HuberRegressor) of y on c over the training set to get a, b, and set the baseline to base = a*c + b. Run the whole existing pipeline (OOF stacking, base_predict, meta) on the residual target r = y - base_tr instead of y, then return meta.predict(base_te) + base_te_prior, where base_te_prior = a*c_te + b. Features are unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual learning on Crippen logP

backlog.spec: Reduce the variance of the LightGBM base learner by averaging several models trained with different seeds. In base_predict, replace the single lgb.train call with a loop over 3 seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with its own lgb_params(...) and bagging_fraction=0.8 and bagging_freq=1 added to the params so the models differ. Average the predictions on Xb and return the mean as p_lgb. This keeps the same stacking interface and only changes how p_lgb is produced.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged LightGBM for variance reduction

backlog.spec: Add a nearest-neighbour base learner that uses the existing Tanimoto matrix. In base_predict, compute S = tanimoto(Fb, Fa) (already available as a helper, and it is cheap). For each row of Xb, take the k=7 most similar training molecules by S, and predict the similarity-weighted mean of ya over those neighbours, with weights S**2 and a small epsilon in the denominator. Return this as an extra column, and update the oof column count in fit_predict from 3 to 4 accordingly. Use argsort on -S, or np.argpartition for speed. This gives the stacker a local-similarity signal that differs from the kernel ridge fit.
backlog.title: Tanimoto kNN regressor as a base learner

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace y with z = sign(y) * log1p(|y|) before the stack is trained (the oof loop, meta Ridge target and base_predict all see z). Invert the final prediction with sign(p) * expm1(|p|) before returning it. Leave the rest of the pipeline unchanged, so the descriptor, Tanimoto and RBF members all train on the transformed scale. The meta-learner is fit on transformed oof predictions, and the inversion happens only at the end.
backlog.title: Signed-log target transform

backlog.spec: In base_predict, add a fourth base learner: catboost.CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, loss_function='MAE', rsm=0.2, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0), fit on Xa, ya and predict Xb. Append p_cb as a fourth column of the returned matrix, and change oof = np.zeros((len(y), 3)) to np.zeros((len(y), 4)). The positive Ridge meta-learner stays. If runtime gets near the limit, reduce iterations to 500.
backlog.title: Add CatBoost as fourth base learner

backlog.spec: logD depends strongly on ionization, so add a small block of substructure counts to the feature matrix. Define about 10 SMARTS patterns: carboxylic acid [CX3](=O)[OX2H1,OX1-], tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide, phenol, aliphatic primary/secondary/tertiary amines (non-amide, non-aniline N with sp3 carbons), amidine/guanidine, pyridine-type aromatic N, and quaternary N. In featurize (or a helper called from fit_predict), compute per-molecule counts with Chem.MolFromSmiles(s).GetSubstructMatches for each pattern and hstack them as float32 columns after the descriptor block. Keep the Tanimoto kernel on the ECFP bits only, as now, and make sure the base_predict slicing for descriptors (Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:]) is updated so the new columns are included in the RBF kernel and the tree models.
backlog.title: Ionizable-group SMARTS count features

backlog.spec: The descriptor block feeding the RBF kernel is currently only mean/std standardised, so heavy-tailed columns such as molecular weight, Ipc and various counts dominate Euclidean distances. In base_predict, replace that standardisation with sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=min(1000, n_train), output_distribution='normal', random_state=seed), fitted on the training descriptor rows and applied to both train and test rows. Afterwards drop any column whose standard deviation is below 1e-9, and keep gamma = 1.0 / (2 * n_remaining_columns). Only the kernel member is affected; the random forest and LightGBM members keep the existing clipped raw descriptors, and the stacking structure is unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-Gauss transform of descriptors before the RBF kernel

backlog.spec: Append three columns to the feature matrix: RDKit Crippen MolLogP, TPSA and the count of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors combined. Compute them from the same mol objects used for descriptors, cache per SMILES as desc_vector does, and clip to the 1st to 99th percentile range like the other descriptors. Keep these columns inside the LightGBM and RF inputs only, so the Tanimoto and RBF kernels still use the same columns as before. This is a small, cheap addition.
backlog.title: Crippen logP and TPSA as a small physchem block

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM objective from regression_l1 to huber with alpha (the delta parameter) set to about 0.5, since logD targets have a range of roughly -1.5 to 4.5 and outliers are common. In lgb_params, set objective='huber' and add alpha=0.5. Huber gives smooth gradients near zero and robustness to outliers. Keep all other settings the same. Also try a second variant with objective='fair' and fair_c=0.5 if the first is not clearly better, but ship only the better one.
backlog.title: Huber objective for the LightGBM learner

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, after computing the meta-learner and base_te once on the full training set, also run the whole base_predict on 4 extra bootstrap-by-scaffold-group resamples (sample groups with replacement, seed-driven). Reuse the same meta weights. Return the median of the 5 stack predictions. Cap the runtime by skipping the inner stacking OOF for the resamples, since the meta weights are reused.
backlog.title: Subagged stack with median aggregate

backlog.spec: Before training, clip the training targets to their 1st and 99th percentiles computed on train_y: y_c = np.clip(y, np.percentile(y, 1), np.percentile(y, 99)). Use y_c everywhere y is used inside fit_predict, including the oof loop and the final base_predict call. Test predictions are not clipped. This is a single line added after y is cast to float64.
backlog.title: Winsorise extreme training targets

backlog.spec: Both the random forest and the LightGBM member are stochastic, and a single draw adds variance on top of the genuine model error. Inside base_predict, fit each of them three times with random_state / seed values seed, seed + 1000 and seed + 2000, and average the three prediction vectors into a single column before returning. To stay inside the ten-minute limit, drop the random forest to 120 trees and LightGBM to 400 rounds so the total tree count is roughly unchanged. The kernel-ridge member is deterministic given its grid search and is left untouched, as is the stacking loop and the meta-learner.
backlog.title: Multi-seed averaging of the stochastic base learners

backlog.spec: Change the settings to N_BITS = 2048 and RADIUS = 3. Since the code slices descriptors as Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:] and the kernel uses Ftr[:, :N_BITS], those slices update automatically. Larger substructures and fewer bit collisions should help both the Tanimoto KRR and the trees. Make no other change. If runtime is too long, lower RF n_estimators from 200 to 150.
backlog.title: Radius-3 ECFP with 2048 bits

memo: Helped: RDKit 2D descriptors (0.7230 to 0.5902), LightGBM with a cheap inner grid (0.5728), FCFP-style Morgan (0.5585), stacking RF, LightGBM and a Tanimoto kernel learner (0.5357), summed Tanimoto+RBF kernel ridge member (0.5062), then grid-searching its lambda and RBF weight (0.4895, incumbent, only 1 run). Did not help: bit filtering (0.7555), bigger Morgan (0.5880), MLP (0.5719), extra fingerprints/counts (MACCS, atom-pair, BRICS, count FPs 0.5087), ionisable SMARTS, 3D descriptors, density weighting (0.5089), xgboost swap (0.5025), DART (0.4914), label propagation (0.5230), product kernel (0.4895, no change), residual linear model (0.4859, within noise). Heavy inner loops caused timeouts and crashes, so watch the 10-minute limit. Next: replicate the incumbent to confirm 0.4895. Then try a better meta-learner or kernel hyperparameters (RBF gamma). Avoid more feature additions and small tweaks.
